name: US–China / Taiwan
summary: Surge to 49 PLA aircraft around Taiwan on 3 Nov; no large-scale exercise announced
state: Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 Chinese military aircraft, six warships and six official ships around Taiwan in the 24 hours to 3 Nov, one of the busiest days this year (TaiwanPlus); reports also describe a large naval mobilisation (SCMP). China has not announced an exercise. China's pause on rare-earth export controls ends on 10 Nov. Normal holds until a declared large-scale drill or incident.
for_you: No direct effect for most people as of 5 Nov. Firms reliant on Taiwanese chips or Taiwan Strait shipping are the most exposed if activity escalates.
rubric_hit: No declared large-scale exercise, blockade or incident; activity elevated = Normal

sources.title: TaiwanPlus — Massive surge in Chinese military activity (3 Nov)
SCMP — Taiwan flags massive PLA naval mobilisation, spike in air sorties

why: The world's two largest economies; a Taiwan crisis would halt most advanced chip supply and risk great-power war.
drivers: PLA exercises, tariffs and tech controls, diplomacy, Taiwan politics, South China Sea incidents.

rubric.alert: Blockade or 'quarantine' of Taiwan, military clash, or severed diplomatic channels.
rubric.watch: Large-scale PLA exercises around Taiwan, major new sanctions/controls, or a naval/air incident.
rubric.normal: Managed relations; dialogue channels open; routine PLA activity.
